title: OpenAI safety leader David Robinson resigns as the team's upheaval mounts
key_facts: David Robinson, a leader on OpenAI's Safety Systems team, has resigned; an OpenAI spokesperson told Business Insider on Friday (2 Oct 2026) that he left last week.
Robinson had previously led OpenAI's policy planning and worked on safety transparency, including system cards (public documents describing a model).
On Thursday (1 Oct 2026) OpenAI said it had 'parted ways' with three researchers who it said violated its policies on sharing sensitive information.
Business Insider ties this to a wave of attention on OpenAI's safety practices after the high-profile Hugging Face security breach and other incidents in which OpenAI says its models misbehaved.
Safety head Johannes Heidecke also left earlier this year.
In early September Robinson wrote on X that things at OpenAI were 'changing significantly by the day' but he did not know 'whether we are changing fast enough'.
quote_evidence: David Robinson, a leader on OpenAI's Safety Systems team, has resigned from the company.
An OpenAI spokesperson told Business Insider on Friday that Robinson left last week, marking yet another moment of upheaval in the company's safety ranks.
The company shared on Thursday that it had "parted ways" with three researchers, saying they had violated its policies for sharing sensitive information.
why_it_matters_hint: Another senior person from OpenAI's safety side has left during a run of safety incidents and staff changes.
event_date: Left 'last week' (exact date not given); confirmed by OpenAI on 2 Oct 2026
